clue.text: Gateway for large number to get aboard wonderful ship

indicators.note: getting aboard means climbing inside a vessel, so the number goes inside the next word

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
ace is slang for excellent
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A boarding gangway for a crowd of passengers joining a splendid liner.
explanation.walkthrough: The hundred climbs inside ACE, which is then followed by the ship to give ACCESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateway is a means of entry, and access is likewise the way in to a place.

clue.text: Let others see expensive coat picked up by driver

indicators.note: something picked up is caught by the ear, so the words are judged by their sound

blocks.note: to show something is to let others see it
a fur coat is a costly garment

explanation.surface: A smart fur coat is collected by the chauffeur so everyone can admire it.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, SHOW FUR is a fair match for the French-derived CHAUFFEUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A chauffeur is a person employed to drive a private car for someone else.

clue.text: Queen's worried about one of horses

indicators.note: worried suggests agitated and disturbed, so these letters are shaken into a new order
about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters wrap round the numeral

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The monarch frets over one of her racehorses.
explanation.definitionFit: Equine is the adjective relating to horses, from the Latin equus.

clue.text: Sets off to Stuart's bash

indicators.note: a bash is a blow, and these words get knocked about into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone heads off to a party being thrown by Stuart.
explanation.walkthrough: Bash looks like a noun meaning party, but here it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To start out is to begin a journey, which is exactly what setting off means.

clue.text: Visit state pupils at home

blocks.note: CA is the abbreviation for California, a US state
L stands for learner, so two of them are pupils
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A school inspector drops in on state-school pupils in their homes.
explanation.walkthrough: State school is a British phrase for a public school, which misleads you into reading the words together.
explanation.definitionFit: To call in is to make a short visit to someone, dropping by on the way.

clue.text: Back in charge, taking car out and about

indicators.note: back tells us to read the abbreviation in the opposite direction
out means disordered or wrong, so the vehicle's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: IC is the abbreviation for in charge
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone back in command takes the car out for a drive around.
explanation.definitionFit: Circa is the Latin word used before dates to mean approximately, the same as about.

clue.text: Nitrogen's good in Merlot bottled for the future

indicators.note: in places the chemical symbol and the grade inside the wine
bottled is slang for drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A winemaker adds nitrogen to Merlot in the bottle so it keeps for years.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottled looks like it describes the wine, but it is slang for drunk and signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something long-term is planned or intended to last over an extended period ahead.

clue.text: Patriarch from Asia running riot gets caught

indicators.note: running riot means out of control, so the continent's letters go wild

blocks.note: taken as written
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A tribal elder from Asia causes a riot and is arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac, son of Abraham and father of Jacob, is one of the three biblical patriarchs.

clue.text: Warrior almost takes old city with a display of great spirit

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the fighter is dropped

blocks.note: a brave is a Native American warrior
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fighter nearly conquers an ancient city in a show of tremendous courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravura is a brilliant, daring performance or manner, a showy demonstration of boldness and flair.

clue.text: Cross with poor casual worker before the start of day

indicators.note: the start of means only the opening letter of the following word is wanted

blocks.note: poor quality is bad
a temp is a temporary worker
ere is an old word for before
the opening letter of day

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed with an incompetent temp who turns up at the crack of dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross looks like part of the surface's annoyance, and it is: it is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross as an adjective means irritable or angry, which matches being in a foul mood.

clue.text: Steal from artist's new bag

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist; the 's means has
N is the abbreviation for new
a sack is a large bag

explanation.surface: A thief pinches a painter's brand-new handbag.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack a place is to plunder or rob it, searching it thoroughly for valuables.

clue.text: Take care of castle, working under one with vision

indicators.note: in a down entry under means placed below, so the working word comes after the eye

blocks.note: a keep is the strongest tower of a castle
an eye is a single organ of sight
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A caretaker looks after a castle while working for a far-sighted boss.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, under means placed below, so the working word comes after the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep an eye on something is to watch over it and look after it.

clue.text: The day's leading entomologist has limited skill with lice treatment

indicators.note: leading means at the front, so the opening letters of the two words are taken
treatment means processing or handling, so the parasites' letters are reworked

blocks.note: the opening letter of day
the opening letter of entomologist
something finite has limits
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion
taken as written

explanation.surface: The leading insect expert of the day turns out to be rather poor at treating head lice.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening word looks like mere scene-setting, but it is the whole definition, a word naming itself grammatically.
explanation.definitionFit: In English grammar the word the is called the definite article, as opposed to a or an.

clue.text: Kisses for old lovers

blocks.note: first meaning: kisses are written as the letter X, and the plural spelt out gives this
second meaning: former partners

explanation.surface: Someone sends kisses to former partners.
explanation.walkthrough: Kisses are written as Xs at the end of a letter, and the plural of the letter X is spelt EXES.
explanation.definitionFit: Exes are former spouses or partners, and the same spelling is the plural name of the letter X.

clue.text: Cheese a little while before sleep's rejected every time

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the final words are read from right to left

blocks.note: a mo is a moment
ZZ is the cartoon sign for sleep
every one is all
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A little cheese snack before bed is always refused.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozzarella is a soft white Italian cheese, traditionally made from buffalo milk.

clue.text: Criss-crossed unknown island and gazed around astride horse

indicators.note: around suggests turned about, so the letters of the verb are reordered
astride means with legs on either side, so the jumbled letters sit either side of the horse

blocks.note: Z is an algebraic unknown
I is the abbreviation for island
taken as written
gee-gee is a childish word for horse

explanation.surface: A rider crosses a mysterious island this way and that, staring about from the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To zigzag is to move in a series of sharp alternate turns, crossing and recrossing a path.

clue.text: Peer's father — sick but not hard to take care of

indicators.note: not hard says the abbreviation for hard is removed from the parent
sick means unwell, so the remaining letters are put out of order

blocks.note: to peer is to look closely
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nobleman's father falls ill and needs nursing.
explanation.walkthrough: Peer looks like a nobleman, but it is the verb meaning look. H is the usual abbreviation for hard, as on pencils.
explanation.definitionFit: To look after someone is to tend them and see to their needs.

clue.text: Knew area could be made to revive again

indicators.note: could be made suggests the letters can be fashioned into something else

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone familiar with a district could help bring it back to life.
explanation.definitionFit: To reawaken is to rouse once more, bringing something back into consciousness or activity.

clue.text: Commission agent's backing money to mature

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the salesman's word is read in reverse

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative, an agent
a cent is a coin
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A salesman's fee depends on financial backing being given time to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: Backing looks like financial support of the money, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A commission is paid as a percentage, a proportion of each sale made.

clue.text: Ordinary fellow describes king in jest

indicators.note: describes in its sense of draw round, as in describing a circle, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: Joe, as in average Joe, is an ordinary man
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An everyman jokingly describes a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Describe can mean trace a line around something, as a compass describes a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A jest is something said for amusement, and a joke is the everyday word for it.

clue.text: Teams of doctors cover our organisation

indicators.note: organisation means arranging, so the letters of the possessive are rearranged
cover means enclose, so the doctors wrap round the other letters

blocks.note: GPs are general practitioners, family doctors
taken as written

explanation.surface: Groups of physicians provide medical cover for a company.
explanation.walkthrough: GP, general practitioner, is the usual British term for a family doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Teams and groups are both sets of people gathered together for a purpose.

clue.text: Coach online

blocks.note: surface reading: a tutor or trainer working over the internet
setter's reading: a passenger vehicle that runs on a rail line

explanation.walkthrough: Online suggests the internet, but read it as on the line: a coach travelling along the tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway carriage is called a coach, and it runs on a railway line.

clue.text: Raise tax on custom working

indicators.note: in a down clue raise means lift upward, so the tax letters are read bottom to top

blocks.note: NI is National Insurance, a British payroll tax
custom and use both mean established practice

explanation.surface: A government increases the duty charged on imported goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Custom suggests customs duty, but here it means habit. On places the raised tax on top of it in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in use is currently operating or being employed, so it is working.

clue.text: Tugs at last sadly sank at sea

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the next word
at sea means confused, so the verb's letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the final letter of sadly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tugboats finally, regrettably, went down in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: Tugs look like boats, but the definition is the verb meaning pulls.
explanation.definitionFit: To yank is to pull with a sudden sharp jerk, which is what tugs means as a verb.

clue.text: Kilometre in, end run injured and wasted

indicators.note: in places the distance unit among the other letters
injured means hurt or damaged, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
K is short for kilometre
taken as written

explanation.surface: A runner hurt in the last kilometre of a race is exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: Wasted looks like tired out after the run, but it is slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasted is slang for heavily intoxicated, so it matches drunken.

clue.text: Greedyguts is large in stomach and a heavyweight

indicators.note: in places the size abbreviation inside the belly word

blocks.note: the gut is the stomach
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a ton is a very heavy weight

explanation.surface: A greedy eater has a big belly and weighs a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Greedyguts is a British playground word for someone who eats too much.
explanation.definitionFit: A glutton is someone who eats to excess, exactly what the childish insult describes.

clue.text: Lapse with catch turned the game

indicators.note: turned means facing the other way, so the joined words are read backwards

blocks.note: a lapse is a moral slip, a sin
to net is to catch

explanation.surface: A dropped catch changes the course of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: Catch suggests cricket, but here it is the net used to catch things.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport, so it is a game, here named with the article.

clue.text: Passion for teacher's indeed unending

indicators.note: unending means losing its last letter, so the act's tail is cut off

blocks.note: sir is what British pupils call a male teacher
read as in deed: a deed, an act, missing its final letter, with the teacher placed in it

explanation.surface: A pupil's crush on a teacher really is endless.
explanation.walkthrough: Indeed must be read as two words, in deed: the teacher sits in a shortened deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Desire is strong longing or wanting, the same feeling as passion.
